title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Ops, Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes (2026)
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the canonical structure, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs site runbook, and the canonical fixes for our top support issues. It is intended for DevEx authors, SDK maintainers, solutions engineers, and on-call support engineers.

Audience
- Internal: SDK authors, technical writers, solutions engineering, developer support.
- External (derived artifacts): customer-facing quickstarts and examples that live in the public docs site.

Document types covered
1) SDK Guides: deep-dive reference with installation, auth, common patterns, and migration notes.
2) Quickstarts & Templates: 5-10 minute getting-started guides and copy-paste templates for common use cases.
3) API Examples: language-specific (Python/Node/Go/Java) runnable snippets and sample payloads.
4) Docs Site Operating Procedures: CI, release cadence, content review, translation, and monitoring.
5) Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes: curated list of recurring support tickets and verified fixes maintained as runbook items.

Standards & Naming Conventions
- File names: short, kebab-case, include year when appropriate. Example: developer-experience-sdk-quickstarts-api-examples-2026.json
- Titles: human readable, include product surface and intent: "SDK Guide: JavaScript 14 Streaming Responses"
- Headers: Use clear H1/H2/H3 hierarchy. Every page must begin with a 1-2 sentence summary and an explicit "Audience" section.
- Code samples: must be runnable, pinned to a tested SDK version (see Release Process).

Core SDK Guide Structure (required sections)
1. Title and one-line summary
2. Audience and pre-requisites (SDK version, API key, platform)
3. Installation and quick verification (commands)
4. Auth and configuration examples (env vars, config blocks)
5. Typical usage patterns with 2-3 complete examples (synchronous, streaming, error handling)
6. Performance and cost guidance (batching, max tokens)
7. Troubleshooting and links to Top Support Issues
8. API reference links and changelog / migration notes

Quickstart & Template Requirements
- Target completion time: 5-10 minutes.
- Must include: copy-paste commands, expected output, and a minimal troubleshooting section.
- Provide both CLI and SDK example when applicable.
- Include a short test prompt that can be used in automated verification (see Docs CI below).

API Examples (canonical languages)
- Provide first-class examples for: Python, JavaScript/Node, Go, and Java.
- Each example must include: request payload, expected response snippet, and an explanation of fields.
- Streaming examples must show how to consume partial responses and include reconnection guidance.

Docs Site Operating Procedures
- Repo & CI: docs/ repo contains markdown + front matter. All PRs must pass: link check, lint (mdxlint), code snippet execution tests (pytest / node test harness), and accessibility checks.
- Release cadence: weekly content release window on Wednesdays 09:00 UTC. Emergency fixes may be hotfixed outside window with approval from DevEx lead.
- Review process: content changes require at least one engineering reviewer and one technical writer reviewer. Sensitive content (security, billing) also requires product or legal review.
- Monitoring & SLOs: docs site uptime SLO = 99.9% monthly. Example verification checks run every 5 minutes from three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast).
- Alerting: PagerDuty DevEx rotation (@devex-oncall) if broken runnable examples or build failures for more than 30 minutes.

CI snippet (example)
```yaml
# docs/.github/workflows/ci.yml (excerpt)
jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install test deps
        run: pip install -r tests/requirements.txt
      - name: Run runnable snippet tests
        run: pytest tests/snippets_test.py --maxfail=1 -q
      - name: Lint markdown
        run: npx mdxlint .
```

Top Support Issues & Canonical Fixes (current priority list)
1) SDK authentication errors ("401 Unauthorized" / missing API key)
   - Symptom: SDK init throws authentication error immediately.
   - Root cause: user set REDWOOD_API_KEY in shell but not exported; or using an expired key.
   - Canonical fix: Verify env var is exported and scoped key is active. Example: `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_...` then run `redwood-cli auth whoami`. Update the quickstart to include `redwood-cli auth whoami` as verification.
2) Streaming disconnects in unstable networks
   - Symptom: partial tokens received then connection drops.
   - Root cause: client-side aggressive timeouts or missing retry/backoff.
   - Canonical fix: update SDK examples to include reconnect logic and exponential backoff (example below). Add note to SDK guide recommending heartbeat ping every 30s for long-lived streams.
3) High latency on batched inference calls
   - Symptom: tail latency > 1s for small requests when batching enabled.
   - Root cause: incorrect batching configuration (batch window too high) or using large model variant for tiny requests.
   - Canonical fix: demonstrate recommended batching settings in docs (batch_window_ms=5-120, max_batch_size=64) and provide sample config YAML.
4) Mismatched model/param names in examples after model rollout
   - Symptom: example payload references model.name that no longer exists.
   - Root cause: outdated examples post rollout.
   - Canonical fix: include a post-release content sweep task in release checklist (see Release Process). Add model aliasing guidance: prefer stable alias `redwood/text-1` over exact hash when possible.

Example canonical troubleshooting template (to be included in every guide)
- Symptom:
- Quick check commands:
- Likely root causes:
- Canonical fix / steps to remediate:
- Links to follow-up docs or support ticket template:

Canonical config table (example)
| Setting | Recommended value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| batch_window_ms | "5-20" | lower values reduce latency but may increase GPU utilization |
| max_batch_size | "32-128" | tune to GPU memory and throughput targets |
| stream_timeout_s | "120" | increase for long-running streams, include client keepalive |

Sample SDK snippet (Python)
```python
from redwood_sdk import Redwood
import os
client = Redwood(api_key=os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY'])
# Simple completion
resp = client.text.generate(model='redwood/text-1', prompt='Write a short haiku about debugging')
print(resp.output_text)
```

Release Process & Versioning
- SDK examples must pin to an SDK minor version that has passed smoke tests. Example: "redwood-sdk>=1.4.0,<1.5.0" in quickstarts.
- For breaking changes: publish migration guide and create redirect from old examples to migration doc.
- Post-release checklist (content owner): run link-check, snippet tests, update changelog entry, and run a content sweep for model name changes.

Ownership & Contacts
- Primary owner: DevEx Docs Team (devex-docs@redwood.ai)
- Secondary: SDK owners per language: python-sdk@redwood.ai, node-sdk@redwood.ai.
- On-call for docs CI/build: PagerDuty: devex-oncall (rotation in team wiki).

Metrics & KPIs
- Runnable snippet success rate >= 98% per month (automated CI).
- Time to first response for docs-related support tickets: 24 hours.
- Docs site uptime SLO: 99.9% monthly.

Appendix: Example exponential backoff (JS)
```js
async function connectWithRetry(connectFn, maxAttempts = 5) {
  let attempt = 0;
  while (attempt < maxAttempts) {
    try {
      return await connectFn();
    } catch (err) {
      attempt++;
      const delay = Math.pow(2, attempt) * 100 + Math.random() * 100;
      await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, delay));
    }
  }
  throw new Error('Max retry attempts reached');
}
```

Maintenance cadence
- Quarterly review of "Top Support Issues" to retire resolved items and add new recurring tickets.
- Annual audit of all quickstarts to validate runnable status and update pinned SDK versions.
